issueSummary: Homepage returns 403 during user impersonation
issueDescription: An administrator impersonating an employee cannot open the homepage. The homepage request returns HTTP 403 because its ACL evaluates the administrator session instead of the impersonated user's permissions. Direct employee login works.
stepsToReproduce: Sign in as an administrator, impersonate an employee with homepage access, and open Home. Observe a blank page and a 403 homepage request in the Network panel. End impersonation and log in directly as the employee; Home loads.

issueSummary: Access denied on Home when acting as an employee
issueDescription: Home displays an empty screen when an admin switches into an employee identity. A Forbidden response is returned by the homepage endpoint. The access rule uses the original session identity rather than the effective impersonated user; ordinary login is unaffected.
stepsToReproduce: Authenticate with an admin account and use Impersonate User to select an employee. Navigate to the homepage and inspect its network request. Verify status 403. Repeat with a normal login for that employee and confirm the page opens.

issueSummary: Impersonated session is blocked by homepage ACL
issueDescription: Employees who can normally view Home lose access when impersonated by an administrator. The homepage ACL does not resolve the impersonation context, producing a 403 Forbidden response and leaving the page blank.
stepsToReproduce: Choose an employee who can access Home through direct sign-in. Log in as admin, impersonate that employee, and reload Home. Check DevTools for a Forbidden response from the homepage service. Exit impersonation and verify direct sign-in succeeds.

issueSummary: Blank homepage after administrator switches user context
issueDescription: Switching from an administrator to an employee through impersonation makes Home inaccessible. Its authorization script checks the wrong session context, so the server rejects the homepage request with HTTP 403. Signing in as the employee without impersonation succeeds.
stepsToReproduce: Open an administrator session, switch to an employee using impersonation, and select Home from navigation. Reload the page and observe no content. Inspect the homepage response for status 403, then compare with a direct employee session.

issueSummary: PDF attachment larger than 10 MB fails to upload
issueDescription: Attaching a PDF larger than 10 MB to a case fails with HTTP 413 Payload Too Large. The upload gateway enforces a 10 MB limit although the application allows 25 MB. Smaller PDFs upload successfully.
stepsToReproduce: Open a case and choose Add Attachment. Select a 12 MB PDF and start uploading. Observe the attachment is missing and the upload request returns 413. Repeat using a 2 MB PDF and confirm success.

issueSummary: Large PDF rejected despite configured attachment allowance
issueDescription: The case attachment uploader accepts files up to 25 MB in its settings, but PDFs above 10 MB are rejected by the proxy. The server responds with 413 and no attachment is created. Files below the proxy limit work.
stepsToReproduce: Navigate to a case, attach a 15 MB PDF, and monitor the upload endpoint in DevTools. Confirm a Payload Too Large response and no saved file. Upload a small PDF to the same case and verify it appears.

issueSummary: Case document upload stops at gateway size restriction
issueDescription: PDF documents between 10 MB and 25 MB cannot be attached to cases. A gateway request-body restriction disagrees with the application's attachment limit and returns HTTP 413. The failure does not occur for smaller documents.
stepsToReproduce: Select an existing case and upload an 18 MB PDF through the attachment control. Wait for the operation to finish and check that no document was added. Inspect the failed request for 413, then retry with a 5 MB PDF.

issueSummary: Attachment service returns Payload Too Large for valid PDFs
issueDescription: A PDF permitted by the 25 MB application limit is blocked when it exceeds 10 MB. The reverse proxy rejects the attachment request with status 413, leaving the case without the file. Small PDF uploads complete normally.
stepsToReproduce: Visit a case detail page and select a 20 MB PDF as an attachment. Submit the upload and inspect the response for HTTP 413. Confirm the file is absent from attachments. Repeat with a 1 MB document and confirm it is saved.

issueSummary: Case search times out when query contains quotation marks
issueDescription: Searching cases using a quoted phrase leaves the loading indicator active until the request times out. The search parser mishandles quotation marks and generates an expensive query. Searching the same words without quotes returns results quickly.
stepsToReproduce: Open Case Search, enter "payment failed" including quotation marks, and submit. Observe prolonged loading followed by a timeout. Remove the quotation marks and repeat; matching cases are returned.

issueSummary: Quoted phrase causes case search to hang
issueDescription: The case search service becomes unresponsive for phrases surrounded by double quotes. Incorrect phrase parsing produces a slow backend query that eventually times out. An unquoted version of the phrase completes normally.
stepsToReproduce: Navigate to the case search screen and search for "delivery delayed" with both quote characters. Wait for the search request to time out. Search for delivery delayed without quotes and confirm results load promptly.

issueSummary: Exact-phrase case lookup never finishes loading
issueDescription: Entering a phrase in quotation marks into case lookup triggers a search timeout instead of results. The quoted-input parser constructs an inefficient database query. The issue disappears when quotation marks are removed.
stepsToReproduce: Access Case Search and enter "account locked" as a quoted phrase. Execute the search and observe the spinner until the timeout error appears. Retry account locked as plain text and verify the search completes.

issueSummary: Selected due date moves back one day after saving
issueDescription: A case due date selected in the Asia/Kolkata timezone displays as the previous calendar day after saving. The date-only value is converted through UTC as a timestamp, shifting the stored date backward.
stepsToReproduce: Set the user timezone to Asia/Kolkata. Open a case, select September 20, 2026 as its due date, and save. Reload the record and observe September 19, 2026 instead of the selected date.

issueSummary: Case deadline changes to previous date on reload
issueDescription: Users configured for Asia/Kolkata find that a saved case deadline is one day earlier than their selection. The application treats a calendar date as a timezone-dependent timestamp during UTC conversion.
stepsToReproduce: Use an account with Asia/Kolkata timezone, edit a case deadline to October 5, 2026, and submit the form. Reopen the case. Confirm the deadline now reads October 4, 2026.

issueSummary: UTC conversion shifts case due date backward
issueDescription: Saving a date-only case deadline from an Asia/Kolkata session changes its calendar day. Converting local midnight to UTC before extracting the date makes the persisted deadline one day too early.
stepsToReproduce: Configure Asia/Kolkata in user preferences. Choose November 12, 2026 in the case due-date picker and save the case. Refresh and check that November 11, 2026 is displayed.

issueSummary: Double-clicking Submit creates two cases
issueDescription: Rapidly clicking Submit twice on the new-case form creates duplicate records. The button remains enabled while the first request is pending and the server accepts both submissions without deduplication.
stepsToReproduce: Open Create Case and fill all required fields. Enable slow network throttling, then double-click Submit before the first request completes. Check the case list and observe two records with identical submitted details.

issueSummary: Repeated form submission produces duplicate case entries
issueDescription: Two fast clicks on the case creation button send two POST requests and save the same case twice. There is no pending-request button lock or server idempotency protection, making duplication easier on slow connections.
stepsToReproduce: Enter details in the new-case form and simulate a slow connection in DevTools. Click Submit twice in quick succession. Inspect two creation requests and verify two cases containing the same information.

issueSummary: New case is saved twice when Submit is pressed rapidly
issueDescription: The creation form permits another submission before the first one finishes. Rapid repeated clicks create two identical cases because the frontend does not disable Submit and the backend does not recognize duplicate requests.
stepsToReproduce: Navigate to New Case, complete required inputs, and throttle the network to Slow 3G. Press Submit twice while the first operation is waiting. Refresh the case list and find two separate records with matching details.

issueSummary: Tab key moves focus outside the open confirmation modal
issueDescription: Keyboard focus escapes the delete-confirmation dialog and reaches controls behind its overlay. The modal has no working focus trap, so Tab does not cycle between the dialog buttons.
stepsToReproduce: Open a case and activate Delete to display the confirmation modal. Move focus to its last button and press Tab. Observe focus entering the underlying page instead of returning to the first modal control.

issueSummary: Delete dialog allows keyboard navigation into background page
issueDescription: The delete confirmation overlay does not contain keyboard focus. Tabbing beyond the final dialog action reaches links on the case page underneath because focus trapping is missing.
stepsToReproduce: Launch the delete confirmation from a case detail page. Use Tab to visit each dialog control, then press Tab again after the last action. Verify a background page link receives focus while the dialog remains open.

issueSummary: Confirmation modal fails to keep focus within its controls
issueDescription: When the delete-case modal is visible, Tab and Shift+Tab can move focus to the obscured case page. The dialog fails to wrap focus between its first and last interactive elements.
stepsToReproduce: Display the delete-case confirmation dialog. Press Tab from the final button and Shift+Tab from the first button. Observe focus leaving the modal for underlying controls instead of cycling within the dialog.
